accuracyChecks.method: Three rounds of 5 random generated items per chapter (50 items each, 150 in all, across bank, practice forms and mocks; round 2 drawn only from computed items) re-solved by hand: every numerical recomputed from the stem data, every fact/MCQ key checked against NCERT Chemistry XII
fixes: relative lowering of vapour pressure: key was computed from the unrounded vapour pressure, so the answer differed by about 0.3% from one worked from the stem; now computed from the printed value
pH/degree of dissociation of weak acids and bases: approximation alpha << 1 used where alpha was about 0.13 (e.g. 0.01 M HCOOH); such cases are now rejected and stems state the assumption
elevation of boiling point items with a negligible elevation (about 0.003 K) are rejected; answer now gives the elevation and the boiling point
sucrose hydrolysis answer now also answers the 'why invert sugar' part
imperative prompts ('Identify the cell') no longer end with a question mark; Greek letters no longer capitalised at the start of answers
'e.g.' feature cues and an inner-transition intro that did not fit the 3d series item reworded; awkward case template switched off for the transition-metal properties table
accuracyChecks.note: Two keys were numerically off (both fixed); no other wrong answers found. Bank regenerated and revalidated after the fixes.
